mainCharacter.name: Pip
mainCharacter.role: Main character; a careful little warehouse forklift
mainCharacter.color: Mint-green body with cream forks, pale yellow mast, and soft navy accents
mainCharacter.bodyShape: Small compact forklift with a rounded cabin, short mast, two cream lifting forks, and no arms or hands
mainCharacter.face: Round friendly blue windshield eyes and a tiny smile on the front panel
mainCharacter.wheels: Four solid dark charcoal tires with cream hubcaps
mainCharacter.accessories: Small navy side mirrors, a pale yellow safety stripe on the mast, and a soft night lantern clipped near the cabin roof

Blanket Crate.role: Supporting prop; a wooden crate of soft bedtime blankets

setting.Sleepy Shelf Warehouse: A calm evening warehouse with low wooden shelves, soft floor lights, stacked blanket crates, wide aisles, and a round night clock on the wall
setting.visualStyle: Warm polished 3D children's illustration, soft rounded forms, clean single-scene compositions, gentle warehouse evening glow, and no readable text

style: Warm polished 3D children's animation illustration, bright friendly lighting, soft rounded forms, true 4:3 landscape single continuous scene. NO text, letters, numbers, badges, logos, watermarks, panels, collage, grid, comic layout, contact sheet, or multi-panel. Vehicles have NO arms, hands, or human limbs. Leave the bottom 25-30% of the frame as soft uncluttered ground/space so a narration panel can overlay later; keep all important subjects above the lower quarter.
continuityRules: Pip keeps the same mint-green body, cream forks, pale yellow mast, blue windshield eyes, four matching wheels, and night lantern on every page.
Pip and every vehicle have no human-like arms or hands; lifting is done only with the cream forks.
The blanket crate stays light pine with lavender, cream, and sky-blue blankets and a purple tag.
The low wooden shelf destination is introduced early and matches on Pages 4 and 11-15.
The crate is wobbly on Pages 4-9 and sits steady on the shelf from Page 11 onward.
The sky/warehouse light progresses from golden evening through soft dusk to quiet night.
Every illustration is one continuous scene with no panels, collage, grid, contact sheet, text, badge, logo, or watermark.
